checks.claim: C1. Original scope, coupling, source fidelity and named-input boundary.
checks.reason: Note §1 lines 31-38 fix d=1, 0<a<1, 0<alpha<=1, the raw kernel |t-s|^-a, and Gamma = c_Gamma|x|^-alpha dx (alpha<1) or c_Gamma delta_0 (alpha=1) with c_Gamma>0 kept. Lines 36-38 state that W is the raw-law noise of the SEMICLASSICAL equation (W), not the original unscaled field, and that the raw driver and Z come from the same W. No source cutoff is assumed measurable from W. I checked W^delta(f)=delta^(a/2-1)W(f(./delta,.)) directly: its covariance is delta^(a-2)·delta^2·delta^(-a)|u-u'|^-a Gamma, which is raw, as line 49 says. The named inputs (lines 15-26) match contract-v3 lines 5-8 exactly, including phase-response Section5(M) lines 302-325 rather than Section 6. I confirmed those lines hold (M) for every T,R>0 with a Bochner L2 proof and no positivity assumption. The local-flow inputs used are the R>=1 mask, F, K via (4.2), the input/output support [-2R-T,2R+T], the kappa_R extension (local-flow lines 211-216), the Young map (5.1)-(5.3), the deterministic base (5.5)-(5.6) and (6.1). The driver inputs used are §§5-6 (common-space tests, C^gamma versions, the little-Hölder space). Direct-event §1 is used for (S)/(W). One citation, to phase-response §4 for the d=1 form of Gamma, lies outside the explicit list; see minor finding 2. Every claimed limit is at fixed delta, r, L (line 52).

checks.claim: C2. Concrete full-product assembly Phi, its bound, separability, Phi(X)=A including constant inputs, joint Gaussian closure, and Bochner b.
checks.reason: I is finite because O=[-2r-L,2r+L] is compact and supp rho_j is in [j-1,j+1]. K:F->E is bounded by (4.2) at fixed r, L. D_rho_j:E->F is bounded because rho_j is a bounded E multiplier and global E embeds in F (local-flow lines 173-176). Bound (3) follows from HS >= operator norm, and Phi(x)(0)=0, so Phi is everywhere linear and continuous into C^theta_0(B(F)) with only a sum bound; nothing claims B(F)-valued separability. The separability proof for h^theta_0 holds: two polygonal paths with the same vertices and nearby breakpoints differ by a Lipschitz function with small sup norm, and interpolation [f]_theta <= 2||f||_inf^(1-theta) Lip(f)^theta makes the difference small; vertices are then approximated in separable HS(E). X_j lies in h^theta_0 because driver lines 285-290 give C^gamma versions, with polygonal convergence in C^theta for gamma>theta. For Phi(X)=A: local-flow lines 213-216 define A(u)w := A(u)(kappa w) for every w in F, including constants. The output lies in O, so sum_{j in I} rho_j y = y. Also rho_j chi_j = rho_j, and global E is never assumed dense in F. Joint Gaussianity of the countably many HS matrix entries with Z holds because every entry is a W-test in the first-chaos closure of the same W (driver lines 233-238). b=E[XZ] exists by Cauchy-Schwarz on separable B, and Phi(b)=E[AZ] because bounded linear maps commute with Bochner integrals.

checks.claim: C3. Raw profile h, its regularity and tails, the strong integral (7), the covariance with Jacobian (8), extension to indicator coordinate kernels, and Phi(b)=sqrt(delta) H_delta.
checks.reason: I checked (8): delta^(a/2-1)∫f(t/delta,x)h(t,x)dtdx = delta^(a/2)∫f(q,x)h(delta q,x)dqdx under t=delta q. Writing h(t)=∫|q|^-a G(t-q)dq with G(s)=Gamma*psi(s) compact in s∈(0,1), only |q|<1 matters for t∈[0,1]. So ∂_t h and ∂_t∂_x h are absolutely convergent and bounded, which gives Lipschitz dependence into C_b^1, hence continuity and strong measurability despite C_b^1 being nonseparable. For Riesz, Gamma*∂^k psi = O((1+|x|)^-alpha) with c_Gamma kept; for white it is compact, so the tails in (6) vanish. Multiplying by zeta_r keeps everything in the admissible class (5.6) with compact support. The coordinate kernel of chi_j A(u) is 1_[0,u](q)·zeta_r(x) times a smooth function of (q,x). This holds because the free wave multipliers cos(tξ), sin(tξ)/ξ and ξ sin(tξ) preserve Schwartz functions, and the E-adjoint factors (1-Δ)^(±1/2) and chi do as well. Approximating the indicator converges in the noise Hilbert norm by dominated convergence, because the kernel |q-q'|^-a Gamma is nonnegative and locally finite. So (8) extends to the literal coordinates and gives E[<X_j(u)e_k,e_l>Z] = g delta^(a/2) <chi_j H_delta(u)e_k,e_l>. Since g delta^(a/2) = delta^((1-a)/2+a/2) = delta^(1/2), (9) holds on global E inputs. Extending (9) to constant inputs also needs finite propagation for H_delta, which is not spelled out; see minor finding 1. Identification goes through coordinates, not a contraction bound.

checks.claim: C4. The Gaussian law identity (10): equivalent probability, finite-dimensional completion of squares including singular covariance, sign and cost, Borel generation, pi-lambda, null sets, v=0.
checks.reason: The representation (xi,Z) =law (TN, z·N) via a PSD square root allows singular covariance, with Tz = Cov(xi,Z) = l(b) and |z|^2 = v. The identity exp(-|n|^2/2 - s z·n - s^2|z|^2/2) = exp(-|n+sz|^2/2) with n'=n+sz gives E[exp(-sZ - s^2v/2) f(l(X)+s l(b))] = E f(l(X)) with no matrix inverse. MINUS density with PLUS shift is correct: tilting by -sZ moves the mean of xi to -s l(b). Taking f=1 gives normalization, and the density is positive and finite, so Q ~ P. On Borel generation: point evaluations and matrix entries are continuous linear functionals. The sup norm and Hölder seminorm of a continuous path are suprema over rational times and pairs (Q∩[0,L] plus {0,L}), and the HS norm is the square root of the sum of squared entries in an E-ONB. So x ↦ ||x-y||_B is coordinate-measurable, balls are cylinder-generated, and separability makes the Borel sigma-algebra equal sigma(coordinates). The pi-lambda argument and monotone convergence then extend to all nonnegative Borel j on all of B, allowing +∞. v=0 forces Z=0 and b=0, so (10) is trivial. Translating by the deterministic s·b stays in B and creates no exceptional set.

checks.claim: C5. The observable J_delta, the retained-residual tilt (13), the noise-only canonical identification, and the original point consumer (14).
checks.reason: J_delta is continuous and nonnegative on all of B for four reasons: Phi is continuous linear, S(L) is bounded on F (local-flow §4), U_A is locally Lipschitz in C^theta on bounded sets (5.3), and ell_phi is bounded on F by (4.2) plus duality. With s=1/sqrt(delta), (9) gives Phi(X + b/sqrt(delta)) = A + H_delta. This is the Young flow with deterministic base A_h, h = zeta_r h(delta q,·), plus g M_r, as local-flow line 324 allows. So the residual g zeta_r W^delta is kept and no nonzero-profile canonical series is assumed. The cost is s^2 v/2 = v/(2 delta), which is correct. E J_delta(X) is finite by the all-moment bounds on the evolution (local-flow lines 294-298), which also makes the weighted side of (13) finite. Mask protection holds: M+L <= (1+M)/delta <= r and zeta_r = 1 on [-r,r]. Then (6.1) applies at horizon L. The time change to slow time works because a fast vertex g delta^(a/2-1) G_((t-t')/delta) W(dt') equals delta^(-1/2) G_((t-t')/delta) W(dt'), which is direct-event's mild vertex for (W), with phase (V, delta V_t) and data e0. Direct-event (S)/(W) then gives the law of u(T,Rx) with R = T delta, and (M) gives (14) with no R^d factor and no positivity assumption. Neither covariance monotonicity nor a global stationary operator is used. Two steps are left implicit and are supplied inside the named scope: the time-change citation (local-flow lines 464-468) and the Bochner-average law transfer; see minor findings 3 and 4.

checks.claim: C7. The four local Lean statements, the negative controls, and the Python probes.
checks.reason: The literal types in types-and-axioms.txt match JointTilt.lean. tilt_exponent is a universal ring identity over r,s,c,v,w. It is exactly the log of E[exp(-sZ - s^2v/2 + r(xi + sc))] = exp(r^2 w/2), using Var(r xi - sZ) = r^2w - 2rsc + s^2v. That matches (10) with j = exp(r l) and the note's MINUS density/PLUS shift; it is not a Gaussian MGF theorem. I checked the residuals by hand: wrong_sign_error leaves 2rsc and wrong_cost_error leaves -s^2v/2. shifted_amplitude has only hypothesis 0<delta and proves delta^((1-a)/2)·delta^(a/2)/√delta = 1 via rpow_add, sqrt_eq_rpow and div_self. That is the real-power amplitude consumed in (9) and (13); no target identity is assumed. All four depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The controls are false at r=s=c=v=w=1: WrongSign evaluates to 2≠0, WrongCost to -1/2≠0, and WrongAmplitude 4/√4 = 2≠1. Each log shows 'unsolved goals ⊢ False' with exit code 1, not an API or setup error. The receipt's original and replay hashes are identical. Reading check_contract.py (A=X, Z=σX+τY, w=1) and check_polynomial.py as source, both encode the same exact algebra, and their JSON values match my hand recomputation (for example 4, -2, -6, -2601/200, -9/8, -40). I did not re-score kernel correctness. The probes add no Gaussian or flow content, and none is claimed.

checks.claim: C8. Honesty, non-vacuity, no hidden gaps or circularity, remaining goal stays open.
checks.reason: Lines 3-8 and §6 (lines 301-316) disclaim everything C8 lists: no event rate, spectral complement/cone/product bound, terminal-growth observable, sharp constant, optimizer-profile map, source-constant map, source-normalization repair, higher-dimensional claim, novelty, whole-paper/circulation clearance or Lean package. No desired analytic result enters as a hypothesis: (10) is proved from finite-dimensional facts, (9) from the covariance computation, and (13)-(14) from named inputs. The four worker-honesty concerns are each addressed by the C2-C5 checks above. Prior inputs remain scoped named inputs. The note does not state non-vacuity (v>0 for nonzero psi, as contract §5 does), but the theorem holds for all v>=0; see minor finding 6.

minor: 1. §3 lines 193-197 extend (9) from global-E inputs to all of F, including constant phases, by 'the bounded operator/cutoff construction'. This needs two facts that are not spelled out: H_delta(u)w = H_delta(u)Kw, and that H_delta(u) has output supported in O. Both follow quickly from accepted finite propagation of the free group (local-flow §4, chi_j S(t)v = chi_j S(t)psi_j v) and supp zeta_r ⊂ [-2r,2r]. Global-E density in F cannot replace them, and the note correctly does not assume it. One explicit sentence would close this.

2. Line 34 cites 'accepted phase-response Section4' for the d=1 form Gamma = c_Gamma|x|^-alpha dx. That section is outside the contract's explicit list. The fact is elementary and is an internal dependency of the named local-flow note (local-flow line 27 lists phase-response as an input), so no stronger analytic input is borrowed. The citation boundary could be stated precisely.

3. Line 283 cites only local-flow (6.1) and direct-event §1 for identifying J_delta(X) with the semiclassical canonical average. This needs the fast-to-slow time change (u = t/delta, cutoff eta/delta ↔ eta, vertex factor g delta^(a/2-1) = delta^(-1/2)). The accepted local-flow §7 lines 464-468 supply it, and I checked the algebra, but the note should cite that passage.

4. The law transfer from direct-event §1, which equates finite lists of fixed-order terminal coefficients, to the Bochner spatial average ∫phi(x)u(T,Rx)dx is left implicit. For (14) only the second moment is needed, which is ∫∫phi phi E[V V] by Bochner/Fubini and follows from two-point equality. Worth one sentence.

5. Notation overlaps: local-flow's (T,R) means (horizon, mask), applied here at T=L, R=r, while direct-event's (T,R) is physical (line 283 versus 285). Line 274 also calls the probability space carrying the semiclassical W 'the original common Gaussian probability space'. The note does distinguish r from the physical R (line 43), but these phrasings risk confusion.
6. Non-vacuity, i.e. v>0 for nonzero psi as in contract §5, is not restated in the note. The tilt is correct for every v>=0, so this affects only the remark, not correctness.

7. Phi(X)=A and the version identities hold almost surely; the qualifier is implicit in lines 100-107. The WrongAmplitude control (delta=4, exponent sum 1) is a generic altered-power check and is not tied to one named plausible error. Both points are presentation only.

limitations: This is an AI review using Read only. It is not human verification and not a novelty audit. I did not run Lean, Python or any build. The compiled-correctness, replay and hash evidence for the four kernel deductions was accepted as the named local input, as instructed. I checked types, statements, applications and the reachability of each control's False by hand arithmetic only. That norm_num reduces √4 to 2 in the pinned Mathlib is inferred from the recorded logs.

The prior accepted notes (interaction-driver §§5-6, local-flow §§3-7, direct-event §1, phase-response §5(M)) were treated as scoped named inputs and were not re-proved. Any defect inside them would carry over to this note's conclusions.

No whole-paper, novelty, circulation or formal Gaussian/Young/SPDE Lean acceptance is claimed or implied. The original sharp target, including spectral/cone/product growth, event rate, optimizer and source-constant map, and higher dimensions, stays open as the note says.
